newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil due $3 higher, Brent 25-30 cents down.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil due $3 higher, Brent 25-30 cents down.

text.p: IPE gas oil is due to open about $3 firmer on Monday, tracking crude's surging rally on Friday which was expected to falter in early trade, dealers said.
IPE June gas oil settled at $173.00 a tonne on Friday afternoon, missing out on a fund-led technical rally which lifted Brent to a new two-month high.
"We should be due about $3 higher against Brent, maybe $1 stronger on the basis of NYMEX heating oil," said a broker.
July Brent, which settled 86 cents up at $20.35 a barrel on Friday, was expected to open 25-30 cents weaker, matching overnight losses on NYMEX ACCESS and Singapore markets.
Brokers said Friday's rally was built on shakey foundations, with many players absent due to industry functions and lacking fundamental support.
"It went up for no particular reason apart from technicals and there's not a lot of support underneath," said one.
Others said the rally became self-fulfilling as institutional funds bought heavily in the New York market and technical targets tumbled.
"There was no way anybody was going to sell it late on Friday," said a broker.
"I see Brent coming back to just under $20 short-term."
U.S. industry data due out later this week would be scrutinised for any evidence of a pick up in gasoline demand as the driving season gets under way.
A further substantial build in U.S. crude stocks, which jumped by a massive seven million barrels the week before last, could prompt a downward correction, dealers said.
European trading volumes were expected to be thin on Monday with much of the continent closed for public holidays.
